primaryQuestion: At fixed AOD550 and identical geometry/common random seed, how much do Shettle aerosol family and season change twilight sky brightness and spectrum?
pairingUnit: comparison group with identical sun depression, target altitude, relative azimuth, observer elevation, AOD550, photon histories and Monte-Carlo seed
secondaryContrasts: S/P ratio state-minus-baseline and log-ratio when both are positive
per-wavelength log radiance ratio when both state and baseline are positive
spectral shape/color differences derived from the frozen wavelength grid
zeroHandling: No epsilon substitution. If a required state or baseline integrated channel is exactly zero, preserve the zero and classify that paired contrast as ZERO_HIT_UNDERCONVERGED_OR_UNDEFINED pending the preregistered numerical rule; never fabricate a finite log ratio.
replicateSummary: For each geometry/sun-depression/AOD/state contrast, summarize the three paired seed replicates using mean log-ratio, sample standard deviation and standard error; preserve all three individual paired contrasts.
spotlightSlices: sunDepressionDeg in {6,8} for sign weakening/reversal check
strongRatioFlag: brightness ratio >= 1.5 or <= 2/3 is a strong candidate effect; ratio >= 2.0 or <= 0.5 is very large. These are interpretation labels, not post-hoc tuning gates.
crossTwilightConsistency: Report whether the same aerosol state that brightens early twilight changes sign or degrades relative behavior at 6-8 degrees; do not choose a preferred family after seeing results.
negativeResultMeaning: Small Shettle-family effects do not rule out aerosols generally; next preregistered suspects are SSA, phase function, particle mixture/size distribution, composition and vertical profile.
downstreamTimingBoundary: First-star timing sensitivity may be evaluated only after the radiance challenge is closed, with stellar transmission and the human visibility/field-factor model frozen and unchanged.
